## Body

Security PASS WITH NOTES for #297 at 2d983f7d218ab635c9f096a1afdcb6e24e524bf9.

No introduced vulnerability was established within C33's same-user trust boundary. The seven-file review was read-only; no source edits or dependency acquisition.

F243: shared-build.sh:359-363 reads a regular, non-symlink stamp with read -r and compares quoted data; stamp content is not executed. The existing eval at line 399 consumes encoded cargo commands, not stamp content. The mkdir lock at line 312 serializes cooperating runs; cargo must succeed at lines 397-401 before the stamp is published at line 407, and copy-out at lines 410-415 remains inside the lock. An ordinary file symlink at the final stamp path is replaced rather than its referent being truncated.

F244: justfile:753-798 refuses missing tmux or a surviving setter before signalling the old daemon. Only PIJ_BOUNCE_UNSAFE=1 overrides. Diagnostics name the missing tool or surviving PID; label metacharacters remain data. These pre-signal refusals are one-directional safety interlocks (brakes). The PATH link farm in build_stamps.rs:686-727 uses PID/counter-scoped scratch names, excludes tmux, and is cleaned on normal return. Recipe execution clears inherited environment at lines 197-207. No introduced secrets, forbidden private identities/machine paths, or manifest/lockfile changes were found.

Nonblocking C34 follow-up: line 407's /bin/mv -f can follow a directory-symlink destination on macOS; the PID-suffixed temporary redirection also is not exclusive creation and has no independent symlink guard. Therefore blanket resistance to all planted stamp-path symlinks is not proven. No normal-use vulnerability within C33 was established. Add file/directory-symlink, preexisting temporary-path, and inert-content cases to the existing shared-build test suite; the current symlink fixture protects the lock owner, not the stamp. Recorded as harness observation security-297/MW-001.
